text.p: These are the headlines selected from Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Unity becomes campaign focus: Political leaders excahnge barbs over their plans to keep Quebec in country.
- Ontario set to overhaul welfare: Changes to affect families, disabled.
- MDs' death role: murder or mercy?: While Nova Scotia prosecutor says the law is quite clear, issue remains blurred.
- Gandhi's widow enters politics: Congress leaders hail decision.
- Mobutu fights on, seeks deal with rebels: Zairian government troops routed, launch last-ditch offensive.
- UN calls Israel to account for methods of interrogation: Torture/Human-rights groups condemn legalizing of 'moderate phusical pressure' to extract information from Palestinians.
- Bre-X fires Felderhof: Embattled company demands chief geologist's resignation; also files for CCAA protection.
- U.S. investors bidding for K mart Canada: Ottawa reviewing a proposal by a group of financial concerns, retailer to buy discount chain.
- Moody's cuts B.C. debt ratings: Agency worried about budget, 'limited fiscal flexibility'.
- Debt problems slam Tee-Comm: Stock plunges as it tries to get financing.
- Bre-X dumps Felderhof: The 'prospector of the year' hands in his resignation as the shatterred company files for creditor protection in wake of Busang fraud.
- George Eaton to resign as retailer's president.
